## Measured: the memory signal is published ~27% of the time — AC4 quantified

Taken 2026-09-06 ~00:30Z, roughly 90 minutes AFTER the stop/start recovery, on a healthy idle host:

```
mem_available_percent    5/18 five-minute buckets = 27% coverage
mcp_healthy (head of script) 12/18                = 66% coverage
```

Same window, same probe run. The difference is position in `observability.sh`: `mcp_healthy`
publishes near line 131, the memory reading later, and the probe is truncated before reaching the
tail (`ignitable-fuchsia-kawala`). This is the same monotone presence-vs-position gradient measured
independently earlier: ~93% at lines 112-213 falling to ~43% at 1463/1511.

**Consequence for this ticket:** the run-up telemetry AC4 asks for does not merely have gaps, it is
absent about three times out of four. On the outage day the metric showed 11-13% available for
hours and then NOTHING for ~5 hours immediately before the wedge. At 27% coverage we would still
miss most of a repeat.

## This reprioritises change 2684

Change 2684 (`Compose the observability probe's time budget`, currently `Verified +1` awaiting
review) has been treated as an alarm-noise fix. It is not — it is the PREREQUISITE for this
ticket's AC2 ("the next occurrence is diagnosable from data alone"). Without it, adding a memory
alarm produces an alarm on a signal that is absent three quarters of the time, which is a
missing-data pager rather than a memory detector.

Recommended sequencing for whoever works this: land 2684 first, confirm coverage rises, THEN add
the `mem_available_percent` threshold alarm. Adding the alarm first inverts the value — it will
fire on absence rather than on memory.

## Also observed, recorded as a value not a finding

The last two readings in the window moved 66% -> 34%. Both are healthy and two points are not a
trend; recorded only because 34% is the first sub-40% reading since recovery and the baseline for
"normal after restart" is not yet established.
